body.p: Applicant submits this Reply in response to the Final Office Action mailed November 7, 2024.
I. Status of the Claims

By this Reply, Applicant amends claims 1, 7, 9, and 17. No new matter has been added by these amendments. Claims 1-20 are pending in this application, with claims 1, 9, and 17 being independent. II. Interview

Applicant thanks Examiner Kretzer and Examiner Messersmith for the courtesies extended during the interview of December 23, 2024. The remarks provided below are consistent with the issues discussed and agreements reached during the interview. In particular, for the reasons provided below, the Examiner agreed that the 101 rejection of claims 1-20 would likely be withdrawn. Ill. Claim Objections.
The Office Action states:

Office Action, page 2. It appears that the Patent Office intends to object to claim 7. In response, Applicant has amended claim 7 to address the objection, as suggested by the Patent Office.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the objection of claim 7 be
reconsidered and withdrawn.
IV. Section 101 Rejections
In the Office Action, claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly
being directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. Without acquiescing to the
merits of the rejection and solely to further prosecution of this application, Applicant has
amended independent claim 1 to recite, in relevant part:
receiving a non-invasive patient-specific three dimensional
anatomic model including a portion of a patient's bowel;
receiving a patient physiological state, the physiological state being
a state different from a resting state;
determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's
bowel modeled by the non-invasive patient-specific three dimensional
anatomic model, based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel and the received physiological state of the patient;
performing a fluid simulation of a blood flow in the received patient- specific three dimensional anatomic model;
determining a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the
portion of the patient's bowel using the fluid simulation, the determined
blood flow demand, and a value of microvascular resistance based on the
received physiological state;
determining adequacy of blood flow to the portion of the patient's
bowel by comparing the determined blood flow characteristic with a
threshold blood flow characteristic; and
generating and displaying (i) an assessment of blood supply
adequacy based on the determined adequacy of blood flow, or (ii) a risk
score defining a risk of disease of the patient's bowel, based on the
comparison.
Independent claims 9 and 17 are amended similarly. Applicant respectfully requests
reconsideration of the Section 101 rejections, and allowance of the instant application.
Applicant submits that the instant claims, at least as amended, are allowable for at least
the following reasons.

Applicant notes that the MPEP has been updated to include the Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance ("2019 PEG"), including limits on what are determined to be "mental processes." For example, MPEP 2106 states:
Examples of claims that do not recite mental processes because
they cannot be practically performed in the human mind include:
- a claim to a method for calculating an absolute position of a GPS receiver and an absolute time of reception of satellite signals,
where the claimed GPS receiver calculated pseudoranges that
estimated the distance from the GPS receiver to a plurality of
satellites, SiRF Tech., 601 F.3d at 1331-33, 94 USPQ2d at 1616- 17;
- a claim to detecting suspicious activity by using network monitors and analyzing network packets, SRI Int'l, 930 F.3d at

As shown above, independent claim 1 recites the use of a non-invasive patient- specific three dimensional anatomic model to determine a blood flow demand of a portion of a patient's bowel based on a determined mass of the portion of the patient's bowel and a physiological state of the patient, and steps of "performing a fluid simulation of a blood flow in the received patient-specific three dimensional anatomic model, determining a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the fluid simulation, the determined blood flow demand, and a value of microvascular resistance based on the received physiological state; determining adequacy of blood flow to the portion of the patient's bowel by comparing the determined blood flow characteristic with a threshold blood flow characteristic; and generating and displaying (i) an assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined adequacy of blood flow, or (ii) a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's bowel,
based on the comparison." These steps cannot practically be performed in the human mind.

For example, the pending claims here are directed toward a method that requires the use of computer simulations (e.g., non-invasive patient-specific three dimensional anatomic model and fluid simulation of a blood flow in the patient- specific three dimensional anatomic model), and substantial data analysis (determining a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the fluid simulation, the determined blood flow demand, and a value of microvascular resistance based on the received physiological state; determining adequacy of blood flow to the portion of the patient's bowel by comparing the determined blood flow characteristic with a threshold blood flow characteristic; generating and displaying (i) an assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined adequacy of blood flow, or (ii) a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's bowel, based on the comparison), and
these processes go far beyond what could be practically performed in the human mind. The human mind is not equipped to practically perform this level of detailed analysis.

Moreover, determining a blood flow characteristic based on the fluid simulation, blood flow demand (that is determined based on the patient's mass and physiological state), and microvascular resistance involves integrating various biological and physical factors, and the process of incorporating these factors into a model and extracting meaningful data involves a level of complex analysis that the human mind cannot practically carry out without assistance from an external computer device.
Accordingly, the steps described in the pending claims involve complex

processes that rely on the use of specialized technologies, and these steps are not easily or practically achievable by the human mind. At least the above-discussed features of amended claim 1 (and similarly amended claims 9 and 17) are therefore similar to those in SRI International or SiRF Technologies discussed in MPEP 2106 above.
In addition, Courts have held that a primary concern of Section 101 is whether

the claims "improperly monopolize 'the basic tools of scientific and technological work."' McRo, Inc. v. BandaiNamco Games America, 837 F.3d 1299 (Fed. Cir. 2016). See also MPEP 2106, which discusses the concern of monopolization repeatedly. The McRo court states that:
[C]Ilaim 1 is limited to a specific process for automatically animating
characters using particular information and techniques and does not preempt approaches that use rules of a different structure or different techniques. See
Morse, 56 U.S. at 113. When looked at as a whole, claim 1 is directed to a
patentable, technological improvement over the existing, manual 3-D animation
techniques. The claim uses the limited rules in a process specifically designed to achieve an improved technological result in conventional industry practice. Alice,
134 S. Ct. at 2358 (citing Diehr, 450 U.S. at 177). Claim 1 of the '576 patent,
therefore, is not directed to an abstract idea.
Similar to McRo, the pending claims are "limited to a specific process for"

automatic assessment of ischemia and related disorders "using particular information and techniques," such as a non-invasive patient-specific three dimensional anatomic model and fluid simulation of a blood flow in the patient-specific three dimensional anatomic model, where the system determines "a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel using the fluid simulation, the determined blood flow demand, and a value of microvascular

resistance based on the received physiological state" and determines "adequacy of blood flow to the portion of the patient's bowel by comparing the determined blood flow characteristic with a threshold blood flow characteristic." When looked at as a whole, the pending claims are directed to a "technological improvement over the existing" medical assessment/simulation techniques. The pending claims use features "in a process specifically designed to achieve an improved technological result in conventional industry practice." Thus, the claims are "not directed to an abstract idea," or at least exhibit "significantly more."

Moreover, as evidenced in part by the lack of 102 or 103 rejection, Applicant submits that the claims clearly are directed to an improvement in computer-related technology, which is all that is required to render the claims statutory under Section 101. Further, the claims recite a "specific way of achieving a desired outcome or end result," which Applicant submits independently render the claims statutory under Section 101.
Applicant further notes that, during the December 23, 2024 interview, the
Examiners also indicate that the proposed amendments would likely overcome the 101 rejection.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the Section 101 rejections, and allowance of the instant application on at least these grounds. V. Conclusion

The Office Action contains characterizations of the claims and the related art with which the applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.
In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to be

understood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.
Applicant respectfully requests that this Reply under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116 be

entered by the Examiner, placing the claims in condition for allowance. The proposed claim amendments do not raise new issues or necessitate the undertaking of any additional search of the art by the Examiner. Therefore, this Reply should allow for immediate action by the Examiner.

Finally, Applicant submits that the entry of this Reply would place the application in better form for appeal, should the Examiner dispute the patentability of the pending claims. Applicant requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
If the examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 2025993307.
